### cylinder3d

This example applies UQ to the flow past a circular cylinder.
Here, the inflow velocity is modeled as a random variable following a uniform distribution $\mathcal{U}[0.8, 1.2]$, introducing $\pm 20\%$ uncertainty.
The simulation setup -- including sampling configuration and postprocessing structure -- is consistent with the `cavity2d` example of this category.
Both Monte Carlo sampling and the stochastic collocation method are supported.
Quantities of interest -- such as the drag coefficient -- are computed for each sample, and statistical moments like the mean and standard deviation are evaluated.

To compute statistics of the drag coefficient, store its values across all samples and apply:

```{.cpp}
uq.mean(drag);
uq.std(drag);
```

Simulation results can be postprocessed and visualized to analyze the sensitivity of flow features to input uncertainty (see @fig-uqCylinder-3d).

::: {#fig-uqCylinder-3d layout-ncol=2}

![Mean $\bar{|\mathbf{u}|}$.](/examples/uncertaintyQuantification/cylinder2d/doc/fig/uqCylinderMean.png){#fig-uqCylinderMean-3d}

![Standard deviation $\sigma(|\mathbf{u}|)$.](/examples/uncertaintyQuantification/cylinder2d/doc/fig/uqCylinderStd.png){#fig-uqCylinderStd-3d}

Mean and standard deviation of the velocity magnitude, computed using the stochastic collocation method with a second-order polynomial expansion and five quadrature points.

:::
